mood.p: Een grijze, natte zaterdag: in het midden van het land valt verspreid zo'n 5 millimeter regen bij maxima rond 14 graden en een matige zuidwestenwind, zondag blijft het wisselvallig. Politiek Den Haag kijkt naar de VS, nu premier Jetten belooft het Internationaal Strafhof steen voor steen te beschermen tegen nieuwe Amerikaanse sancties. Forenzen met de streekbus houden woensdag rekening met een landelijke staking.

global.h3: Russian strike on buses in Kramatorsk kills at least 30
global.summary: A Russian attack on two buses in the frontline city of Kramatorsk killed at least 30 people, part of a day in which at least 41 Ukrainians died nationwide.
body: Two buses were hit on a street in Kramatorsk in Donetsk oblast on Thursday, leaving at least 30 dead and 18 wounded, according to local authorities. Prosecutors released images of bodies and debris around the burnt-out shell of one vehicle.

Ukrainian officials said Russian attacks across the country killed at least 41 people and injured 67 over 24 hours, with 35 deaths in Donetsk oblast alone and glide bombs hitting homes in Zaporizhzhia. Russia also launched 136 drones overnight, of which air defences downed or suppressed 114.

global.h3: Ukraine strike on Donetsk HQ kills record 20 Russian officers
global.summary: Independent monitors say Ukrainian missiles killed 20 Russian officers, including seven colonels, at command posts in occupied Donetsk.
body: Russian outlet Mediazona reported that a Ukrainian missile strike on the headquarters of Russia's Central Military District and its 41st Combined Arms Army killed 20 officers. Eighteen died on the spot and two later succumbed to injuries.

The dead included seven colonels, six lieutenant colonels and five majors, the highest officer toll from a single attack that monitors have recorded. Kyiv has stepped up long-range strikes on command and logistics targets in recent weeks.

global.h3: Trump pledges no Iran strikes before 3 November midterms
global.summary: Trump said talks with Tehran were productive and ruled out attacks until after the US vote, sending oil prices lower.
body: President Donald Trump said late on Thursday that Washington would not attack Iran before the 3 November midterm elections, citing productive discussions with the Islamic Republic. Oil prices slipped on Friday as fears over Gulf supply eased.

US media have reported that the Pentagon has drawn up strike plans and that Trump has told aides he expects a new bombing campaign after the vote. The Kremlin said Trump welcomed Russian efforts toward an Iran settlement, while Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed a strike on an LPG carrier near the Strait of Hormuz.

global.h3: Houthi missiles kill three at Riyadh airport, Saudi coalition hits back
global.summary: A Saudia pilot was among three people killed in Houthi strikes on King Khalid International Airport, prompting a large coalition offensive in Yemen.
body: Saudi aviation authorities said attacks on Riyadh's main airport on Thursday killed Saudia captain Hamoud Ali Alkalthami and two other Saudi citizens and wounded people of several nationalities. Diplomats sheltered in place and a Saudia aircraft was damaged before the airport reopened.

The Houthis said the strikes avenged Saudi raids on the airports in Sanaa and Hodeidah and warned airlines that Saudi airspace outside Mecca and Medina is a target. The Saudi-led coalition responded with what it called a large-scale operation, claiming 136 Houthi military targets destroyed.

global.h3: Ethiopia and Eritrea trade invasion charges over Tigray
global.summary: Addis Ababa told the UN Security Council that Eritrea has launched an all-out invasion, while Asmara says it faces a war of aggression.
body: Ethiopian Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos wrote to the Security Council that Eritrean troops had pushed up to 60km into Tigray. Witnesses placed Eritrean units around Adigrat and a foreign security source estimated 5,000 to 8,000 soldiers inside Ethiopia.

Ethiopian drones have struck the Eritrean forces, which Addis Ababa accuses of backing the TPLF. Federal troops entered Mekelle without a fight last weekend as the rebels withdrew, and the two neighbours cut diplomatic ties last week.

global.h3: Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize for upholding international law
global.summary: The 85-year-old South African jurist, a former ICC and Rwanda tribunal judge, was honoured for holding states and leaders to account.
body: The Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the 2026 prize to Navi Pillay, who defended Nelson Mandela as an anti-apartheid lawyer and later presided over the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda. She sat on the ICC appeals chamber from 2003 to 2008 before becoming UN human rights chief.

Pillay most recently chaired the UN inquiry that concluded Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. The committee said judges and international legal institutions are under political attack, and the award carries 12 million Swedish kronor, around 1.07 million euros.

global.h3: US sanctions the International Criminal Court itself
global.summary: Rubio announced a ban on transactions with the ICC, the first time Washington has targeted the institution rather than its staff.
body: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the measures would cut off the court's resources, blocking its US property and barring funds, goods or services to it. Temporary exemptions cover maintenance, technology and pensions while member states seek a diplomatic fix.

Washington had already sanctioned ICC judges and prosecutors over the Afghanistan probe and the warrant for Benjamin Netanyahu, who thanked the US. Deputy prosecutor Nazhat Shameem Khan condemned the move, and the court, which has about 900 staff, urged its members to step up support.

global.h3: Ukraine, Europe and US envoys meet in Miami on ending the war
global.summary: Witkoff and Kushner host Ukrainian, E3, EU and NATO officials on Friday and Saturday, with Russia absent.
body: The US special envoys are hosting two days of talks in Miami with a Ukrainian team that includes Kyrylo Budanov and Rustem Umerov. National security advisers from France, Germany and the UK attend along with the European Commission and NATO's Geoffrey van Leeuwen.

Washington said the agenda covers security guarantees and a post-war prosperity plan. Kyiv hopes to secure a limited ceasefire covering the Black Sea, energy infrastructure or both, and Zelensky said the US has floated trilateral talks with Russia by the end of October.

global.h3: Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin as US fuel prices soar
global.summary: Russia will ship more than 4 million tonnes of diesel to world markets, and the US Treasury waived sanctions on it until April 2027.
body: After a call with Vladimir Putin, Trump said Russia would supply over 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately, 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes after that, with 3 million more depending on refinery repairs. A Treasury general licence suspends sanctions on Russian diesel through April 2027.

US diesel averages 6.27 dollars a gallon according to AAA, as Ukrainian drone strikes on refineries forced Moscow to halt exports. Zelensky said the easing plays into Russia's hands and critics argue it clashes with US sanctions law.

global.h3: UK and Germany ratify Kensington defence treaty in Berlin
global.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Chancellor Friedrich Merz exchanged ratification papers for the first German-British mutual defence pact since 1945.
body: Merz hosted Burnham at the Chancellery on 8 October, where the two sides formally brought the Kensington Treaty into force. It commits both countries to assist each other if attacked and to hold close dialogue on strategic issues including nuclear threats.

The treaty forms one leg of a London, Paris and Berlin security triangle. It also covers joint defence exports such as Boxer vehicles and Typhoon jets and a plan to develop a deep precision strike missile within a decade.

global.h3: India raises rates for first time since 2023 as inflation climbs
global.summary: The Reserve Bank of India lifted its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% and signalled more hikes may follow.
body: The RBI joined other major central banks in tightening after retail inflation rose for 10 straight months to 4.8% in August, above its 4% target. The move matched economist expectations.
Governor Sanjay Malhotra said cuts are off the table for now and the next step can only be a hike or a pause. HSBC and Goldman Sachs expect another increase in December.

global.h3: Hurricane Isaias slams Florida Panhandle as Category 2
global.summary: The season's first Atlantic hurricane came ashore near Destin with 105 mph winds, cutting power to over 500,000 customers.
body: Isaias made landfall near Destin on Friday evening, the first US hurricane landfall since Milton exactly two years ago. A flash flood emergency was issued for Destin, Fort Walton Beach and coastal Okaloosa County, and Florida declared an emergency in more than a third of its counties.

More than half a million homes and businesses in Florida and Alabama lost power. The storm is forecast to weaken over Alabama and the Tennessee Valley on Saturday, with rain spreading to more than 15 eastern states, and some Gulf oil wells paused output.

global.h3: Magnitude 7.7 quake in Panama triggers regional tsunami alerts
global.summary: A powerful earthquake off Panama's Pacific coast shook the capital and prompted tsunami warnings from Guatemala to Chile.
body: The USGS placed the epicentre about 10km southwest of Pitaloza Arriba. The US National Weather Service issued tsunami warnings for Panama, Colombia, Ecuador, Nicaragua and Guatemala, and Chile's navy issued its own alert.

In Penonome a historic tower collapsed and balconies fell from a residential block, while Panama City residents fled into the streets. Schools were closed and President Jose Raul Mulino appealed for calm, after deadly quakes earlier this year in Venezuela and Colombia.

global.h3: Gaza ceasefire exists in name only, over 100 NGOs warn
global.summary: A year after the US-backed truce, aid groups say Israeli fire has killed more than 1,400 Palestinians, including at least 327 children.
body: Amnesty International, the Norwegian Refugee Council, Save the Children, Oxfam and dozens of other groups said Israeli forces still kill and injure Palestinians daily. Aid restrictions are preventing families from recovering, they said.

More than 74,000 Palestinians have been killed since October 2023 and about 80% of structures in the enclave are damaged. On Thursday Israeli forces shot dead at least one Palestinian in central Gaza camps and shelled areas of Khan Younis.

global.h3: Cars torched as anti-migrant riots hit Soweto and Durban
global.summary: Some 24 vehicles were burned and foreign-owned shops looted in protests over a court ruling on asylum seekers.
body: Police said 10 cars were set alight in Johannesburg's Soweto and 14 in Durban, where three people were arrested and officers fired rubber bullets. Fresh clashes broke out in Durban on Friday and violence also flared outside the Constitutional Court.

Protesters object to a July ruling that removed procedural barriers to claiming asylum, including for people who entered irregularly. The government blamed deliberate disinformation about the judgment and vowed to prosecute those responsible.

global.h3: Maduro and wife charged with torture conspiracy in New York
global.summary: A new count accuses the former Venezuelan leader and Cilia Flores of directing abuse of opponents, including three US citizens.
body: The indictment filed in Manhattan federal court adds conspiracy to commit torture to existing drug trafficking charges. Prosecutors say the scheme ran from 1999 to 2025 and involved waterboarding, rape and beatings by military and intelligence officials.

They allege Maduro personally ordered harsher treatment of a defiant detained officer. The couple, held in Brooklyn's Metropolitan Detention Center, have pleaded not guilty to the drug charges and face trial on 1 June 2027.

global.h3: ICE shooting of Bronx man with child in car sparks protests
global.summary: Federal agents shot Oscar Bergal during an arrest in Marble Hill while his five-year-old sat in the back seat.
body: DHS said Bergal, a 28-year-old Dominican national with a criminal conviction, refused to leave his car and rammed two ICE vehicles before officers fired, grazing his neck. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said agents did not know a child was inside.

The incident drew protests and condemnation from city leaders, while federal officials used it to attack New York's sanctuary policies. NYPD body camera footage of the aftermath has since been released.

netherlands.h3: Netherlands vows to protect ICC as US sanctions the court
netherlands.summary: Prime minister Rob Jetten pledged to defend the Hague-based court stone by stone hours before Washington targeted the institution itself.
body: Foreign minister Tom Berendsen called the US measures an undesirable new escalation and said the Netherlands stands behind the court. The sanctions cut the ICC off from American companies, including financial and technology providers.

The move came on the same day former ICC judge Navi Pillay won the Nobel Peace Prize. As host state, the Netherlands is also facing a Russian request to extradite nine ICC officials convicted in absentia in Moscow.

netherlands.h3: Russia asks NL to extradite ICC president Akane
netherlands.summary: Moscow wants nine ICC officials handed over for their role in the arrest warrant against Vladimir Putin.
body: Russian prosecutors requested the extradition of court president Tomoko Akane and eight colleagues, sentenced in absentia in December to terms of 3.5 to 15 years. The ICC warrant concerns the alleged unlawful deportation of children from occupied Ukraine.
Japan, Akane's home country, called the request regrettable and the measures unjust. The US has separately sanctioned 13 court staff, Akane among them, over the Gaza investigation.

netherlands.h3: Rainbow flag to fly over parliament for first time on Sunday
netherlands.summary: MPs voted 90 to 36 to overrule the presidium and raise the flag for Coming Out Day.
body: Parliament's presidium had dropped the plan after objections led by the SGP, whose MP Diederik van Dijk called it an activist symbol. Pro MP Kati Piri then tabled a motion backing LGBTI rights and an inclusive workplace.
Van Dijk forced a roll-call vote late on Thursday, so MPs who had already gone home had to return to The Hague. The motion passed comfortably.

netherlands.h3: Yeşilgöz now calls Russia the enemy, policy stays the same
netherlands.summary: The defence minister changed her wording during the defence budget debate but said it does not signal a shift in security policy.
body: Dilan Yeşilgöz told NOS that sabotage, drone incidents and intimidation across Europe meant the threat must be named plainly. She stressed the Netherlands is not at war and will not suddenly change course.
She described a new reality in which Putin is testing NATO's strength. In August the cabinet published a draft law giving the AIVD and MIVD sweeping new powers against Russia, China and Iran.

netherlands.h3: MPs want faster terror-glorification law after Dam banner
netherlands.summary: A 'We support Hamas' banner carried onto the Dam on 7 October was judged legal, prompting calls to speed up a pending bill.
body: About 150 people joined the march, some chanting in praise of 7 October, and police stopped them heading to the Jewish quarter. Mayor Femke Halsema called it shocking but lawful, while JA21 and SGP MPs criticised the lack of intervention.

Justice minister David van Weel's bill would create three offences, including public support for banned terror groups, with up to two years in prison. Peace group PAX warns it could be used against activists and journalists.

netherlands.h3: Regional bus drivers to strike nationwide on Wednesday
netherlands.summary: FNV and CNV called a 24-hour walkout covering 13,000 workers and threaten weekly action days if employers do not move.
body: The strike hits regional services run by Arriva, EBS, Qbuzz, Keolis, Transdev and RET, but not city transport in Amsterdam, Rotterdam or The Hague. The collective agreement expired on 1 July and talks collapsed after eight rounds.
An ultimatum to employers' group VWOV lapsed without reply this week. The unions say future strike dates will be announced at short notice.

netherlands.h3: Home buyers gain bargaining room as listings jump 24%
netherlands.summary: NVM says fewer homes sell above asking price as former rentals flood the market, though the average price still rose to 503,000 euros.
body: Just under two-thirds of homes sold between mid-June and mid-September went over the asking price, down from 71% a year earlier. Some 39,000 homes were listed with NVM agents, 24% more than last year, while sales held at about 41,700.

Prices rose 1.8% nationally but only 0.6% in Greater Amsterdam and dipped around Haarlem, Leiden and Zeeland. Much of the extra supply comes from landlords selling apartments, which shrinks the rental market.

netherlands.h3: Up to 11,000 homes bought with forged mortgage papers
netherlands.summary: An unpublished FEC report says criminal groups use fake pay slips and tax returns to acquire housing.
body: NOS reported that between 6,000 and 11,000 Dutch homes were bought with forged documents in recent years, according to a report that has sat with the justice ministry for over six months. Gangs use the properties for money laundering, illegal letting, labour exploitation and drug crime.
Banking association chair Medy van der Laan told MPs the fraud is growing and asked for banks and notaries to verify income with the tax office. Pro MP Hanneke Mutluer wants the report published.

netherlands.h3: Customs chief warns cuts come as cocaine seizures rise 20%
netherlands.summary: Nanette van Schelven told MPs her agency faces budget cuts while drug gangs keep finding new smuggling methods.
body: Customs seized 19,332 kilos of cocaine in the first half of 2026, up from 16,104 kilos a year earlier and close to last year's full total of about 24,500 kilos. It also intercepted over 106 million illegal cigarettes.

Because customs is not formally part of the security sector, it misses out on extra security funding despite a 2027 budget of nearly 982 million euros. Van Schelven said efficiency gains alone cannot close the gap.

netherlands.h3: Only licensed medicinal cannabis grower Bedrocan goes bust
netherlands.summary: A Groningen court declared the firm bankrupt, leaving around 7,000 patients facing a switch to imported products.
body: Bedrocan, based in Veendam with its main site in Emmeloord and about 70 staff, lost its state contract at the start of the year. A law letting growers sell directly to pharmacies will not take effect until 1 July 2028.
The state Bureau for Medicinal Cannabis holds a limited stockpile and will move to imports during 2027. Patients include people with MS, severe pain and some forms of epilepsy.

netherlands.h3: Groningen venues ban smart glasses over privacy fears
netherlands.summary: Around 30 museums, festivals and clubs say camera glasses threaten the privacy and safety of visitors and artists.
body: Signatories include the Groninger Museum, Groninger Archieven, Noorderlicht and the Grand Theatre. Optician chain Hans Anders stopped selling Meta camera glasses last week after pressure from privacy campaigners.

Privacy watchdog AP says sharing footage without consent breaches GDPR and the Consumentenbond warns the recording light can be covered. MPs want a full ban, but the cabinet prefers narrower restrictions.

netherlands.h3: Maastricht region plans 30 care zones to fight loneliness
netherlands.summary: Insurers CZ and VGZ are putting 33.4 million euros into neighbourhoods that help older people live at home longer.
body: The Deltaplan Maastricht Heuvelland brings together councils, insurers, hospitals and residents to combine care, activities and accessible housing. Nineteen of the 30 zones are being developed and the rest should open next year.
Chair Petra Lamberts told NOS that loneliness predicts future care needs. Shared living rooms and group activities are meant to keep people active and less reliant on nursing homes.

netherlands.h3: Report says old transgender law caused profound harm
netherlands.summary: Radboud University researchers found the 1985 to 2014 rules required sterilisation and, until 2001, forced some people to divorce.
body: The study, titled An Inhuman Law and commissioned by the education ministry, drew on 28 interviews with trans and intersex people. Until 2001 applicants had to be unmarried, and until 2014 they had to be permanently infertile to change legal gender.
Participants described years of negotiating with doctors and officials at the cost of their own wellbeing. Some 2,000 people are thought to have been affected, the Volkskrant reported.
